description: Every classic (server-rendered) page route and the V2 (React, /v2) route that replaces it. Source of truth for the classic to V2 edge redirect and for 'open this page in classic'. Read by ui_routing.py and turned into application/v2_ui/src/lib/generated/uiRouteMap.ts by scripts/build_ui_route_map.py. Documented in docs/explanation/features/V2_CLASSIC_PAGE_PARITY.md.

routes.plan_ref: Phase 4 (signed-out and no-role states stay server-rendered by design)
routes.notes: index.html renders three states: signed out, signed in without the User or Admin role (access denied message, Request Access, sign in with another account) and signed in with an app role. V2 home covers only the last one, and the /v2 shell requires the User role, so the first two are always served by the server: the classic interface renders index.html and the modern interface renders templates/modern/landing.html (V2 styling, no classic navigation). That is what stays handed off, by design. The redirect applies to signed-in app users only, and only when the V2 bundle exists. With ENABLE_AUTO_LOGIN_ON_INDEX a signed-out visitor is sent to /login.

V2 reads conversationId (and the older conversation_id), m365_pending_action, chat_link, the document hand-off keys (search_documents, doc_scope, document_id, document_ids, tags, group_id, workspace_id) and the saved prompt keys (prompt, prompt_scope, prompt_scope_id); classic spells the prompt key prompt_id or promptId. Classic-only keys that V2 ignores and the redirect drops: workspace with openSearch and scope=public (public directory chat buttons), openPrompt, feature_action, classification, and m365_request_id with m365_auth (the full-page Microsoft 365 sign-in return: V2 signs in from a popup and resumes the paused request in the page, so it reads neither from the address). Changing a conversation's scope lock (ScopeLockControl) and the generated artifact actions Add to Workspace and Create PowerPoint (GeneratedArtifactActions) are native in V2.

V2's WorkflowActivityPage reads the classic query contract (conversationId, workflowId, runId, scope, groupId), so every existing link maps one to one; classic also accepts group_id for the group, which the redirect renames to groupId.
Chat file upload endpoint, shared by both interfaces: V2 posts to it from lib/endpoints.ts. It is an API, not a page.

Legacy citation viewer that returns a PDF extract of up to three pages around the requested page (doc_id and page). V2 has its own citation viewers, so it is not ported; the only caller is static/js/chat/chat-citations.js.
Returns a stored document for inline preview (doc_id and page). Not ported: V2 has its own citation and document viewers, and no JavaScript in the application calls this route.
Renders conversations.html, which does not exist, so the route raises TemplateNotFound. lib/latestFeatureShortcuts.ts already treats /conversations as the chat page. Candidate for removal.
Renders chat.html, which does not exist (the live page is chats.html), so the route raises TemplateNotFound. Candidate for removal.

Fragments and feature_action values map to V2 sections with the same tables lib/latestFeatureShortcuts.ts uses. V2's Documents explorer shows the 'Update older documents' notice for personal documents too and calls the same route as classic (POST /api/documents/upgrade_legacy). Not mapped: document_id (V2 has no per-document link, so notices open the document list) and tab=agents with new_agent=1 (V2 uses /workspace/agents/new).

Classic works on the active group. V2 /groups opens the active group (or asks you to choose one), /groups/:groupId opens a named group, and a V2 group page makes the group it shows the active one. The group Documents section upgrades legacy documents natively (POST /api/groups/<id>/documents/upgrade_legacy), so the 'Classic tools' button is gone. Query keys and fragments (document_id, group_id, tab=group-agents) are not mapped; lib/notificationLinks.ts opens the group's documents section when the notice names the group.
Classic form handler that sets the active group and redirects to /group_workspaces. V2 switches groups with PATCH /api/groups/setActive, so it is not ported.
Redirects to the Profile Groups tab; needs enable_group_workspaces. The template my_groups.html is unused (dead).

V2 sections Members, Settings, Activity and Statistics cover the manage page. The owner deletes the group natively (the document count is read again before the delete, then DELETE /api/groups/<id>), and the Owner and Admins of an inactive, locked or unknown-status group keep all four sections; adding a member stays closed there, as in classic.

V2 has a native Tags section for a public workspace and upgrades its legacy documents natively (POST /api/public-workspaces/<id>/documents/upgrade_legacy), so the classic hand-offs are gone. Nothing in the classic page reads a query key; the ?workspace= links the public directory writes are ignored, so none are mapped.

V2 sections Members, Settings, Activity and Statistics cover the manage page. The owner deletes natively (the document count is read again, then DELETE /api/public_workspaces/<id>). The Owner and Admins of an inactive, locked or unknown-status workspace keep Members, Settings and Activity, and every stored role keeps Statistics. Deliberate differences: in those statuses V2 keeps the profile and logo read-only, withholds adding members and changing roles (the V2 routes refuse them, classic allows them), keeps Identities and Sync closed for inactive and unknown workspaces, and does not show a DocumentManager the read-only member list.
The chat buttons on the classic page link to /chats with workspace, openSearch and scope=public; V2's 'Chat with all public' uses /chat?public_workspace_selection=all.
Classic form handler that sets the active public workspace and redirects to /public_workspaces. V2 uses PATCH /api/public_workspaces/setActive, so it is not ported.
Redirects to the Profile Public workspaces tab; needs enable_public_workspaces. The template my_public_workspaces.html is unused (dead).

Classic opens on Stats and V2 on Preferences (a deliberate difference), so a link without a tab keeps V2's default. Classic tab settings is V2 Preferences and public-workspaces is Public. V2's Settings page refreshes the profile photo from Microsoft Graph too (Refresh photo). Not mapped: the full-page Microsoft 365 return flags m365_chat_connection and m365_connection (V2 reads the saved connection from the API, so the connected state does not need the address), and the fragments of other settings cards (for example #speech-settings). The two Microsoft 365 fragments are rewritten by V2 itself after the redirect, because a server never sees a fragment (lib/classicLinks.ts).
Redirects to the Profile Feedback tab; needs enable_user_feedback. The template my_feedback.html is unused (dead).
Redirects to the Profile Violations tab. The template my_safety_violations.html is unused (dead).
The V2 Review center replaced this page; App.tsx keeps /admin/feedback-review as a redirect to the same workbench. Needs enable_user_feedback and the feedback reviewer role.

The V2 Review center replaced this page; App.tsx keeps /admin/safety-violations as a redirect to the same workbench. The classic fragment #unchecked-chat-content (linked from the content safety and content screening admin panes) has its own V2 page, /admin/review/safety/unchecked, which this row does not map.

V2 draws the sections from admin_settings_nav.py and saves with PATCH /api/v2/admin/settings; the classic POST form exists only in classic. Global Identities, global agents and actions (with Duplicate) and administrator-managed file sources are native. Deliberate differences: the classic single chat endpoint's own fields (AI Connections replace them) and the informational Standard citations card have no V2 version, and a link to either opens the classic page in a new tab. Every V2 link to the classic admin page names the tab and carries ui=classic, so it is not redirected back. Classic ?tab= and #fragment (tab and section ids) are not mapped; V2 resolves them at run time (lib/latestFeatures.ts, resolveAdminActionTarget).

V2 draws the dashboard, users, groups, public workspaces and activity logs sections, and recalculates the user and group figures from a strip above them (Refresh data, with the last refresh and the automatic refresh status; the refresh route covers users and groups, and public workspace figures are read from stored records). Classic tab ids are not mapped.

m365_approval and support_export are what the server writes into notices; the V2 page turns them into /approvals/m365/<id> and /approvals/support-exports/<id>. #agent-template-approvals opens the admin-only Agent templates category. V2 also accepts approval_id and group_id, which classic never reads.

V2 opens a review from scan_id; scope_type and scope_id are carried because V2 builds links with them (lib/approvalsApi.ts, contentReviewPath) although the page ignores them today. Classic ?tab=policy and ?tab=jobs are not mapped; V2 shows the policy controls on the same page.
Needs enable_semantic_kernel.
Needs enable_support_menu and enable_support_latest_features.
Needs enable_support_menu, enable_support_send_feedback and a recipient email.

V2's NotificationsPage is the full list with the All, Unread and Read filter, search, page sizes and numbered paging, kept in the address as ?status=&q=&page=&per_page=. The classic page reads no query keys, so none are mapped.

routes.plan_ref: Phase 8 (UI_INTERFACE_SELECTION.md; the pre-sign-in terms interstitial stays server-rendered by design)
routes.notes: V2's page serves signed-in users (/v2/terms-of-use with /api/v2/terms-of-use). Before sign-in, /login sends visitors who have not accepted to the server-rendered interstitial. That state stays handed off to the backend because every /v2 page needs a session, but now has a policy-selected modern/terms_of_use.html presentation as well as the legacy template. The redirect applies to signed-in app users only. next is the return path; the server validates it (normalize_terms_of_use_return_path) and the registry carries it only when it is a same-site path.
Shared form target of the classic and modern standalone interstitials. It records acceptance made before sign-in, so it stays server-side in both interfaces; V2 posts to /api/v2/terms-of-use/accept.

Shared form target of the classic and modern standalone interstitials. It ends the session and redirects to the configured decline URL, with or without a session, so it stays server-side; V2 posts to /api/v2/terms-of-use/decline.

Login only, not user_required, because a suspended or blocked user must still reach it. V2 serves its page at /v2/access-restricted (its own login-only route) and reads /api/v2/access-restriction; App.tsx renders it by path, not through a <Route>.
Starts Microsoft Entra sign-in; with teams=true and Teams SSO enabled it renders the Teams sign-in page (login.html). Must stay server-rendered in both interfaces.
Clears the session and signs out of Microsoft Entra (or App Service Easy Auth). V2 links to it with a plain anchor.
Clears the local session only, then redirects to the configured home destination (used by the idle timeout).

OAuth redirect URI of the application. It also finishes the Microsoft 365 chat and workflow sign-ins whose state carries their prefix; those end on m365_connection_result.html or redirect to fixed classic URLs (CLASSIC_* in route_backend_m365.py).
Token redirect URI for API clients. It does not start a browser session.
Creates a session from a validated CI app-only bearer token (404 unless ENABLE_CI_BEARER_SESSION_AUTH is on). Not a page.
Exchanges a Teams SSO assertion for a SimpleChat session (404 unless ENABLE_TEAMS_SSO is on). Not a page.

Microsoft 365 sign-in callback kept for deployments that registered it; new sign-ins return to /getAToken. A popup sign-in (how V2 connects) reports to its opener through m365_connection_result.html; a full-page sign-in redirects to fixed classic URLs (CLASSIC_* in route_backend_m365.py). Those are ordinary classic page URLs, so the classic to V2 redirect carries them into V2 and V2 rewrites their fragments itself; no server-side page_url() helper is needed (docs/explanation/features/V2_INTERFACE_SELECTION_PREREQUISITES.md).

Trusted deployer pages (HTML or Python-backed). V2 shows one in a page of its own at /custom/:slug (CustomPageHost), framing a chrome-less same-origin copy that this route renders for /custom/<slug>?embed=1, so a request carrying embed=1 is never redirected (classic_only_query). The URL alone does not say whether V2 can host the page, so the redirect also checks it: the page must be in the user's navigation, embeddable, not ask to open in its own tab, and not be open to any signed-in user (functions_ui_redirect.custom_page_opens_in_modern_ui). Those pages exist for people without the app role, whom /v2 refuses, so they stay classic, rendered chrome-less in the modern interface.
The familiar .html alias of /custom/<slug>; it renders the same page, so it maps to the same V2 route (V2's address has no .html) and the redirect applies the same checks.
Serves a declared asset of a custom page, after the page's own access check. A static endpoint for the page, not a page.

Public example policy page that visitors can read before they sign in, linked from the default landing text, so it must stay server-rendered in both interfaces. The classic interface renders acceptable_use_policy.html (classic chrome); the modern interface renders templates/modern/acceptable_use_policy.html, which has the V2 look and no classic navigation. It needs no V2 route, and the Terms of Use gate exempts it.
Serves static/robots.txt under an obscured name.
Serves static/favicon.ico. V2 points its own icon link at the administrator's branding instead.
Serves classic JavaScript modules, with the JavaScript MIME type for .mjs files.
Interactive API documentation (only when enable_swagger is on). A developer tool that is the same in both interfaces.
OpenAPI specification as JSON (only when enable_swagger is on). A developer endpoint, not a page.
OpenAPI specification as YAML (only when enable_swagger is on). A developer endpoint, not a page.
